stem: In Salesforce, what is the closest equivalent of a table in a database?
explanation: An object is a table that stores one kind of thing. Records are its rows and fields are its columns. A page layout only arranges how a record is displayed.

stem: An admin creates a custom object labelled Installation. What will the API name end with?
explanation: Custom objects and custom fields get the __c suffix. (__x is used for external objects.)

stem: Which field type should store a customer's choice of exactly one option from a fixed list?
explanation: A picklist offers a fixed list and enforces consistent values. Text would let people type anything, which makes reporting messy.

stem: Which statement about a formula field is true?

options.text: It is calculated automatically and users cannot type into it
Users can edit it on the record page
It stores a value that only changes when a user saves the record
It can only be created on custom objects

explanation: A formula field is read-only and calculated from other fields. It can be created on standard and custom objects.

stem: On which side of a master-detail relationship can you create a roll-up summary field?
explanation: Roll-up summaries summarise child records, so they live on the master object.

stem: Which of these is NOT an available roll-up summary type?
explanation: Roll-up summary fields support COUNT, SUM, MIN and MAX. There is no AVERAGE roll-up.

stem: A parent record in a master-detail relationship is deleted. What happens to its detail records?

options.text: They stay and the lookup is cleared
They move to the recycle bin owner

explanation: Master-detail relationships cascade delete: deleting the master deletes its detail records.

stem: Which relationship type lets a child record exist without a parent by default?
explanation: A lookup relationship is optional unless you make the field required. A master-detail always requires a parent.

stem: How do you model a many-to-many relationship between Installations and Installers?

options.text: A junction object with two master-detail relationships
A lookup field on each object that points to the other
A formula field on Installation that lists the installers
A roll-up summary field on Installer that counts installations

explanation: A junction object with two master-detail relationships represents each pairing, giving you many-to-many.

stem: Which TWO statements are true of a master-detail relationship? (Choose 2)

options.text: The detail record inherits sharing and security from the master
Deleting the master deletes its detail records
The detail record keeps its own independent owner

explanation: Detail records inherit sharing from the master and are cascade deleted with it. They have no independent owner and the master is always required.

stem: A custom object is the detail (child) object in master-detail relationships. What is the maximum number of master-detail relationships it can have?
explanation: A custom object can be the detail in at most two master-detail relationships, which is what makes junction objects possible. (An object can be the master in many.)

stem: A validation rule's formula evaluates to TRUE. What happens?

options.text: The save is blocked and the error message is shown
The record is saved and flagged for review

explanation: Validation rule formulas return TRUE when the data is invalid, which blocks the save.

stem: Which function checks the selected value of a picklist field inside a validation rule?
explanation: Picklist values cannot be compared with = in formulas. Use ISPICKVAL(field, "value").

stem: A validation rule prevents a Completed installation without a completion date. Where does it also apply?

options.text: Data imports, flows and Apex that save the record, not only the UI
Only when a user edits the record from the Lightning page
Only when the record is saved through the mobile app
Only for System Administrators who edit records

explanation: Validation rules fire whenever a record is saved, including imports, automation and API calls.

objective: Use record types and page layouts
stem: What can record types control for different users of the same object?

options.text: Available picklist values and the page layout
Only the object's API name, which each record type changes
The order in which sharing rules are evaluated for the object
Which fields are encrypted when the record is saved

explanation: Record types let different users see different picklist values and page layouts, and on some objects different business processes.

objective: Use record types and page layouts
stem: Which setting lets two Opportunity record types use different sets of stages?
explanation: A sales process defines the Opportunity stages. Each Opportunity record type is linked to one.

objective: Use record types and page layouts
stem: A field is required only on the page layout. In which situation can a record still be saved with the field empty?

options.text: When data is loaded through an import
When a user edits from the web page
When a user clicks Save on the layout

explanation: Layout requirements are enforced only on that screen. To enforce it everywhere, make the field itself required or use a validation rule.

objective: Use record types and page layouts
stem: A field appears on the page layout, but field-level security hides it from a user's profile. What does the user see?

options.text: The field is visible but empty
The field is visible only to the owner

explanation: Field-level security takes precedence. If FLS hides the field, the user does not see it, even if it is on the layout.

objective: Use record types and page layouts
stem: Which TWO can make a record type available to a user? (Choose 2)
explanation: Record type availability is granted through profiles and permission sets. Roles and public groups control record access, not record types.

stem: On which object is a hierarchical relationship field available?
explanation: A hierarchical relationship is a special lookup that is available only on the User object, for example Manager.

stem: Before you can convert a lookup relationship to a master-detail, what must be true?

options.text: Every existing record must have a value in the lookup field
The object must have no page layouts that include the field
The parent must be a standard object, not a custom one
All users must be logged out while the change is made

explanation: A master-detail field is always required, so existing records must already have a parent value before converting.

stem: Which of these can an admin never delete?

options.text: A custom field with no references
A custom object with no data

explanation: Standard fields cannot be deleted. Custom fields and objects can, subject to references.

stem: For roughly how long can a deleted custom field be restored?
explanation: Deleted custom fields stay in the Deleted Fields list for about 15 days, then are permanently erased.

stem: An admin tries to delete a custom field that is used in a validation rule. What happens?

options.text: The delete is blocked until the reference is removed
The rule is disabled and the field is deleted

explanation: A field referenced by a formula, validation rule, flow or similar cannot be deleted until the references are removed.

stem: Which change to a field is safest for existing integrations?

options.text: Deleting it and recreating it with a new name

explanation: A label is only what users see. Changing the API name or deleting a field can break integrations, reports and code that reference it.

stem: Which THREE are valid Salesforce field types? (Choose 3)
explanation: Currency, Checkbox and Geolocation are standard field types. Toggle Switch and Decimal Text do not exist.

stem: In a dependent picklist, which field types can act as the controlling field?
explanation: A controlling field must be a picklist or a checkbox. The dependent field must be a picklist.

stem: What is the main benefit of a global value set?

options.text: One list of values can be reused across many picklist fields
It encrypts the picklist values stored on the records
It limits a picklist field to ten values only
It makes a picklist dependent on another picklist field

explanation: A global value set is defined once and shared by multiple picklists, so changes happen in one place.

stem: What does a lookup filter do?

options.text: Limits which records users can choose in a lookup field
Hides the lookup field from reports for some users
Converts a lookup relationship into a master-detail
Filters list views by owner for each user

explanation: A lookup filter restricts the records available to select in a lookup, for example only active installers.

stem: Khanyisa Solar wants the total kW of all installations to appear automatically on each Account, without code. What should the admin build?

options.text: A master-detail from Installation to Account with a roll-up summary on Account
A lookup from Installation to Account with a formula on Account
A text field filled in by users

explanation: Roll-up summary fields work only when the child is related to the parent by master-detail. A formula cannot summarise many child records.

stem: A user deletes an Account and all of its Installation records disappear too. The most likely cause is:

options.text: A master-detail relationship between Installation and Account
A lookup relationship with the clear-value option
A validation rule on the Installation object
A record type setting on the Account object

explanation: Master-detail cascade deletes detail records with their master. A custom lookup would normally clear the value or block the delete, depending on how it is configured.

objective: Use record types and page layouts
stem: You must guarantee a field is populated for records created by the UI, imports and integrations. What is the most reliable approach?

options.text: Mark the field as required in its field definition
Make it required on the page layout
Add it to the compact layout
Add an instruction in the field help text

explanation: Field-level Required is enforced everywhere. Layout and help text apply only to the UI or give no enforcement.

stem: Two product lines need different picklist values for Stage and different page layouts. What should the admin use?

options.text: Record types with a page layout assignment
A formula field that returns the right layout name for each line
A validation rule that checks the stage on every save
A list view that filters opportunities by product line

explanation: Record types control picklist values and, with layout assignments, which layout each group sees.

stem: A field must be required only when Status equals Closed. Which is correct?

options.text: Make the field required on the layout

explanation: A required field is always required. A validation rule can enforce a condition.

stem: A manager wants the Installation page to show a Discount Reason field only when Type equals Commercial. Which is the best fit?

options.text: A conditional visibility rule in Dynamic Forms
A validation rule that hides the field until a value is entered
A new profile for users who need to see the field
A record type for every discount reason value

explanation: Dynamic Forms can show fields only when conditions are met, without separate layouts.

stem: A picklist for Model must show only values that fit the selected Product Family. Which feature fits?
explanation: Dependent picklists show values based on a controlling field.

stem: Installation needs a count of its related Jobs shown on the parent. The relationship is master-detail. Which is the simplest option?

options.text: A scheduled flow that counts the jobs every night
An Apex trigger that counts the jobs when they change
A report on Jobs grouped by the installation

explanation: Roll-up summary fields count and total child records for the master record with no code.
